A5.2  DeltaNet Setting

DeltaNet’s update is

𝑺t+1=𝑺t−βt​(𝑺t​𝒌t−𝒗t)​𝒌t⊤=𝑺t​(𝑰−βt​𝒌t​𝒌t⊤)+βt​𝒗t​𝒌t⊤,\bm{S}_{t+1}\;=\;\bm{S}_{t}\;-\;\beta_{t}\big(\bm{S}_{t}\bm{k}_{t}-\bm{v}_{t}\big)\bm{k}_{t}^{\top}\;=\;\bm{S}_{t}\big(\bm{I}-\beta_{t}\bm{k}_{t}\bm{k}_{t}^{\top}\big)\;+\;\beta_{t}\,\bm{v}_{t}\bm{k}_{t}^{\top}\,, (A138)

and Gated DeltaNet’s is the same with 𝑺t\bm{S}_{t} replaced by ft​𝑺t\mathrm{f}_{t}\bm{S}_{t} in the first term. Two features are immediate. First, (A138) is affine in 𝑺t\bm{S}_{t}, so the pair (memory, random input) generates a Markov chain of exactly the type analyzed for the Kronecker Delta Rule. Second, and decisively, the memory is acted on from the right only, so the rows of 𝑺\bm{S} do not mix. Transposing (A138),

𝑺t+1⊤=(𝑰−βt​𝒌t​𝒌t⊤)​𝑺t⊤+βt​𝒌t​𝒗t⊤,\bm{S}_{t+1}^{\top}\;=\;\big(\bm{I}-\beta_{t}\bm{k}_{t}\bm{k}_{t}^{\top}\big)\bm{S}_{t}^{\top}\;+\;\beta_{t}\,\bm{k}_{t}\bm{v}_{t}^{\top}\,, (A139)

and reading off the jj-th column, i.e. the jj-th row 𝒔(j):=𝑺⊤​𝒆j\bm{s}^{(j)}:=\bm{S}^{\top}\bm{e}_{j} of 𝑺\bm{S},

𝒔t+1(j)=(𝑰−βt𝒌t𝒌t⊤)𝒔t(j)+βtvt,j𝒌t,j=1,…,d.\bm{s}^{(j)}_{t+1}\;=\;\big(\bm{I}-\beta_{t}\bm{k}_{t}\bm{k}_{t}^{\top}\big)\,\bm{s}^{(j)}_{t}\;+\;\beta_{t}\,v_{t,j}\,\bm{k}_{t}\,,\qquad j=1,\dots,d\,. (A140)

We will use later the key covariance matrix 𝑲¯=E⁡[𝒌​𝒌⊤]\bar{\bm{K}}=\mathbf{\mathrm{E}}[\bm{k}\bm{k}^{\top}] and the value covariance matrix 𝑽¯=E⁡[𝒗​𝒗⊤]\bar{\bm{V}}=\mathbf{\mathrm{E}}[\bm{v}\bm{v}^{\top}].

The structural correspondence.

Equation (A140) is identical to the vectorized KronLSTM recursion 𝒔t+1=(𝑰−β​𝒂t​𝒂t⊤)​𝒔t+β​ct​𝒂t\bm{s}_{t+1}=(\bm{I}-\beta\bm{a}_{t}\bm{a}_{t}^{\top})\bm{s}_{t}+\beta c_{t}\bm{a}_{t} under the substitution

𝒂t=𝒌t⊗𝒗t⟼𝒌t,ct⟼vt,j,ℝd2⟼ℝd.\bm{a}_{t}\;=\;\bm{k}_{t}\otimes\bm{v}_{t}\;\;\longmapsto\;\;\bm{k}_{t}\,,\qquad c_{t}\;\;\longmapsto\;\;v_{t,j}\,,\qquad\mathbb{R}^{d^{2}}\;\;\longmapsto\;\;\mathbb{R}^{d}\,. (A141)

DeltaNet is thus dd independent copies of the same scalar delta rule all driven by a common key 𝒌t\bm{k}_{t} and differing only in their scalar targets vt,jv_{t,j}. KronLSTM is a single copy of that rule on a d2d^{2}-dimensional state with the richer direction 𝒌t⊗𝒗t\bm{k}_{t}\otimes\bm{v}_{t}. Neither is a generalization of the other; both are Kaczmarz/LMS iterations, which is why the same theory covers both.

A5.3  KronLSTM Retention of the Initial Memory

We consider KronLSTM and the Kronecker Delta Rule. We ask how much of an initial memory 𝒔0\bm{s}_{0} survives after tt steps. The mean recursion (A136) is affine, so it separates the two contributions exactly. Writing 𝑴:=𝑰−β​𝑨¯\bm{M}:=\bm{I}-\beta\bar{\bm{A}} and unrolling,

E⁡[𝒔t]=𝑴t​𝒔0+β​∑τ=0t−1𝑴τ​𝒃¯=𝑴t​𝒔0⏟initial memory+(𝑰−𝑴t)​𝒔LS⏟acquired memory,\mathbf{\mathrm{E}}\big[\bm{s}_{t}\big]\;=\;\bm{M}^{t}\bm{s}_{0}\;+\;\beta\sum_{\tau=0}^{t-1}\bm{M}^{\tau}\,\bar{\bm{b}}\;=\;\underbrace{\bm{M}^{t}\,\bm{s}_{0}}_{\text{initial memory}}\;+\;\underbrace{\big(\bm{I}-\bm{M}^{t}\big)\,\bm{s}^{\mathrm{L}\mathrm{S}}}_{\text{acquired memory}}\,, (A142)

where the geometric sum was evaluated with β​∑τ=0t−1𝑴τ=(𝑰−𝑴t)​(𝑰−𝑴)−1​β=(𝑰−𝑴t)​𝑨¯−1\beta\sum_{\tau=0}^{t-1}\bm{M}^{\tau}=(\bm{I}-\bm{M}^{t})(\bm{I}-\bm{M})^{-1}\beta=(\bm{I}-\bm{M}^{t})\bar{\bm{A}}^{-1} and 𝑨¯−1​𝒃¯=𝒔LS\bar{\bm{A}}^{-1}\bar{\bm{b}}=\bm{s}^{\mathrm{L}\mathrm{S}}; equivalently E⁡[𝒔t]−𝒔LS=𝑴t​(𝒔0−𝒔LS)\mathbf{\mathrm{E}}[\bm{s}_{t}]-\bm{s}^{\mathrm{L}\mathrm{S}}=\bm{M}^{t}(\bm{s}_{0}-\bm{s}^{\mathrm{L}\mathrm{S}}), which is the error recursion (A134) in the mean. Everything in E⁡[𝒔t]\mathbf{\mathrm{E}}[\bm{s}_{t}] that depends on 𝒔0\bm{s}_{0} sits in the first term, and it depends on it linearly. The natural measure of retention is therefore the read-out of that term along the stored direction,

ℛt​(𝒔0):=𝒔0⊤​∂E⁡[𝒔t]∂𝒔0​𝒔0=𝒔0⊤​𝑴t​𝒔0,‖𝒔0‖=1,\mathcal{R}_{t}(\bm{s}_{0})\;:=\;\bm{s}_{0}^{\top}\frac{\partial\,\mathbf{\mathrm{E}}[\bm{s}_{t}]}{\partial\,\bm{s}_{0}}\,\bm{s}_{0}\;=\;\bm{s}_{0}^{\top}\bm{M}^{t}\,\bm{s}_{0}\,,\qquad\left\lVert\bm{s}_{0}\right\rVert=1\,, (A143)

the fraction of a unit initial memory still legible after tt steps. It equals 11 at t=0t=0 and requires no assumption relating 𝒔0\bm{s}_{0} to 𝒔LS\bm{s}^{\mathrm{L}\mathrm{S}}: the acquired term is filtered out by differentiation rather than by orthogonality.

Proposition A2 (Retention rate).

Assume κ:=β​Amax2≤1\kappa:=\beta\,A_{\max}^{2}\leq 1 with Amax2=maxi⁡‖𝐚i‖2A_{\max}^{2}=\max_{i}\left\lVert\bm{a}_{i}\right\rVert^{2}, so that β​λmax​(𝐀¯)≤1\beta\,\lambda_{\max}(\bar{\bm{A}})\leq 1 and 𝐌⪰𝟎\bm{M}\succeq\bm{0}. Then for every unit 𝐬0\bm{s}_{0}

(1−β​λmax​(𝑨¯))t≤ℛt​(𝒔0)≤(1−β​λmin​(𝑨¯))t,\big(1-\beta\,\lambda_{\max}(\bar{\bm{A}})\big)^{t}\;\;\leq\;\;\mathcal{R}_{t}(\bm{s}_{0})\;\;\leq\;\;\big(1-\beta\,\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{A}})\big)^{t}\,, (A144)

both bounds being attained, at the corresponding eigenvectors of 𝐀¯\bar{\bm{A}}. Averaged over a uniformly random unit 𝐬0\bm{s}_{0} the retention is exactly the normalized trace,

E𝒔0​[ℛt​(𝒔0)]=Tr​𝑴td2=1d2​∑k=1d2(1−β​λk​(𝑨¯))t,\mathbf{\mathrm{E}}_{\bm{s}_{0}}\big[\mathcal{R}_{t}(\bm{s}_{0})\big]\;=\;\frac{\mathbf{\mathrm{Tr}}\,\bm{M}^{t}}{d^{2}}\;=\;\frac{1}{d^{2}}\sum_{k=1}^{d^{2}}\big(1-\beta\,\lambda_{k}(\bar{\bm{A}})\big)^{t}\,, (A145)

and the retention horizon — the number of steps after which the slowest mode has decayed to 1/e1/\mathrm{e} — is t1/e=1/log⁡(1−β​λmin​(𝐀¯))−1≃1/(β​λmin​(𝐀¯))t_{1/\mathrm{e}}=1/\log\big(1-\beta\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{A}})\big)^{-1}\simeq 1/\big(\beta\,\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{A}})\big).

Proof.

𝑨¯\bar{\bm{A}} is symmetric, so 𝑴=𝑰−β​𝑨¯\bm{M}=\bm{I}-\beta\bar{\bm{A}} is symmetric with eigenvalues 1−β​λk​(𝑨¯)∈[0,1)1-\beta\lambda_{k}(\bar{\bm{A}})\in[0,1) under β​λmax≤1\beta\lambda_{\max}\leq 1, hence 𝑴t\bm{M}^{t} is symmetric positive semidefinite with eigenvalues (1−β​λk)t(1-\beta\lambda_{k})^{t}. Equation (A144) is the Rayleigh-quotient bound for 𝑴t\bm{M}^{t}, with equality on its extreme eigenvectors, which are those of 𝑨¯\bar{\bm{A}} for λmax\lambda_{\max} and λmin\lambda_{\min} respectively. For (A145), E⁡[𝒔0​𝒔0⊤]=𝑰/d2\mathbf{\mathrm{E}}[\bm{s}_{0}\bm{s}_{0}^{\top}]=\bm{I}/d^{2} for a uniform unit vector in ℝd2\mathbb{R}^{d^{2}}, so E⁡[𝒔0⊤​𝑴t​𝒔0]=Tr⁡(𝑴t​E​[𝒔0​𝒔0⊤])=Tr⁡(𝑴t)/d2\mathbf{\mathrm{E}}[\bm{s}_{0}^{\top}\bm{M}^{t}\bm{s}_{0}]=\mathbf{\mathrm{Tr}}(\bm{M}^{t}\mathbf{\mathrm{E}}[\bm{s}_{0}\bm{s}_{0}^{\top}])=\mathbf{\mathrm{Tr}}(\bm{M}^{t})/d^{2}. The step-size condition holds because λmax​(𝑨¯)≤maxi⁡‖𝒂i‖2=Amax2\lambda_{\max}(\bar{\bm{A}})\leq\max_{i}\left\lVert\bm{a}_{i}\right\rVert^{2}=A_{\max}^{2}, 𝑨¯\bar{\bm{A}} being a convex combination of the 𝒂i​𝒂i⊤\bm{a}_{i}\bm{a}_{i}^{\top}. ∎

A5.4  DeltaNet Retention of the Initial Memory

Corollary A6 (DeltaNet retention).

By the row decomposition (A140), DeltaNet’s mean memory obeys E⁡[𝐒t]=𝐒0​𝐍t+𝐒LS​(𝐈−𝐍t)\mathbf{\mathrm{E}}[\bm{S}_{t}]=\bm{S}_{0}\bm{N}^{t}+\bm{S}^{\mathrm{L}\mathrm{S}}(\bm{I}-\bm{N}^{t}) with 𝐍:=𝐈−β​𝐊¯\bm{N}:=\bm{I}-\beta\bar{\bm{K}}, so with ℛt​(𝐒0):=⟨𝐒0,𝐒0​𝐍t⟩F\mathcal{R}_{t}(\bm{S}_{0}):={{\left\langle\bm{S}_{0},\bm{S}_{0}\bm{N}^{t}\right\rangle}}_{\mathrm{F}} and ‖𝐒0‖F=1\left\lVert\bm{S}_{0}\right\rVert_{\mathrm{F}}=1,

(1−β​λmax​(𝑲¯))t≤ℛt​(𝑺0)≤(1−β​λmin​(𝑲¯))t,E𝑺0​[ℛt]=Tr​𝑵td,\big(1-\beta\,\lambda_{\max}(\bar{\bm{K}})\big)^{t}\;\;\leq\;\;\mathcal{R}_{t}(\bm{S}_{0})\;\;\leq\;\;\big(1-\beta\,\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{K}})\big)^{t}\,,\qquad\mathbf{\mathrm{E}}_{\bm{S}_{0}}\big[\mathcal{R}_{t}\big]\;=\;\frac{\mathbf{\mathrm{Tr}}\,\bm{N}^{t}}{d}\,, (A146)

A5.5  KronLSTM Retains Longer than DeltaNet

The two retention rates are governed by the spectra of 𝑨¯\bar{\bm{A}} and 𝑲¯\bar{\bm{K}}, and for independent keys and values these are related exactly.

Proposition A3 (Spectral comparison).

Let 𝐤\bm{k} and 𝐯\bm{v} be independent and let 𝐕¯:=E⁡[𝐯​𝐯⊤]\bar{\bm{V}}:=\mathbf{\mathrm{E}}[\bm{v}\bm{v}^{\top}]. Then 𝐀¯=𝐊¯⊗𝐕¯\bar{\bm{A}}=\bar{\bm{K}}\otimes\bar{\bm{V}}, so the eigenvalues of 𝐀¯\bar{\bm{A}} are the d2d^{2} pairwise products of those of 𝐊¯\bar{\bm{K}} and 𝐕¯\bar{\bm{V}}, and in particular λmin​(𝐀¯)=λmin​(𝐊¯)​λmin​(𝐕¯)\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{A}})=\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{K}})\,\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{V}}) and λmax​(𝐀¯)=λmax​(𝐊¯)​λmax​(𝐕¯)\lambda_{\max}(\bar{\bm{A}})=\lambda_{\max}(\bar{\bm{K}})\,\lambda_{\max}(\bar{\bm{V}}). If the values are ℓ2\ell_{2}-normalized, ‖𝐯‖=1\left\lVert\bm{v}\right\rVert=1, then Tr​𝐕¯=1\mathbf{\mathrm{Tr}}\bar{\bm{V}}=1 and hence

λmin​(𝑨¯)≤λmin​(𝑲¯)d,λmax​(𝑨¯)≤λmax​(𝑲¯),\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{A}})\;\;\leq\;\;\frac{\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{K}})}{d}\,,\qquad\lambda_{\max}(\bar{\bm{A}})\;\;\leq\;\;\lambda_{\max}(\bar{\bm{K}})\,, (A147)

with equality in the first when the values are isotropic, 𝐕¯=𝐈/d\bar{\bm{V}}=\bm{I}/d.

Proof.

𝒂​𝒂⊤=(𝒌⊗𝒗)​(𝒌⊗𝒗)⊤=𝒌​𝒌⊤⊗𝒗​𝒗⊤\bm{a}\bm{a}^{\top}=(\bm{k}\otimes\bm{v})(\bm{k}\otimes\bm{v})^{\top}=\bm{k}\bm{k}^{\top}\otimes\bm{v}\bm{v}^{\top} by the mixed-product rule, and independence factorizes the expectation. The spectrum of a Kronecker product of symmetric matrices is the set of pairwise products. For normalized values λmin​(𝑽¯)≤Tr​𝑽¯/d=1/d\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{V}})\leq\mathbf{\mathrm{Tr}}\bar{\bm{V}}/d=1/d and λmax​(𝑽¯)≤Tr​𝑽¯=1\lambda_{\max}(\bar{\bm{V}})\leq\mathbf{\mathrm{Tr}}\bar{\bm{V}}=1, giving (A147); isotropy forces 𝑽¯=𝑰/d\bar{\bm{V}}=\bm{I}/d and the first inequality becomes an equality. ∎

Because keys and values are ℓ2\ell_{2}-normalized in the KronLSTM block, ‖𝒂i‖2=‖𝒌i‖2​‖𝒗i‖2=1=‖𝒌i‖2\left\lVert\bm{a}_{i}\right\rVert^{2}=\left\lVert\bm{k}_{i}\right\rVert^{2}\left\lVert\bm{v}_{i}\right\rVert^{2}=1=\left\lVert\bm{k}_{i}\right\rVert^{2}, so both models admit exactly the same step sizes β≤1\beta\leq 1 and the comparison at equal β\beta is well posed. Under Propositions A2 and A3:

  • •

    The slowest mode decays dd times more slowly. KronLSTM’s worst-case retention (1−β​λmin​(𝑨¯))t(1-\beta\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{A}}))^{t} dominates DeltaNet’s (1−β​λmin​(𝑲¯))t(1-\beta\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{K}}))^{t}, and the retention horizons are

    t1/eKronLSTM≃1β​λmin​(𝑨¯)≥dβ​λmin​(𝑲¯)=d​t1/eDeltaNet,t_{1/\mathrm{e}}^{\text{KronLSTM}}\;\simeq\;\frac{1}{\beta\,\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{A}})}\;\;\geq\;\;\frac{d}{\beta\,\lambda_{\min}(\bar{\bm{K}})}\;=\;d\;t_{1/\mathrm{e}}^{\text{DeltaNet}}\,, (A148)

    a factor dd in context length at which a stored association is still legible, with equality for isotropic values.

  • •

    No mode decays faster. By the second half of (A147), λmax​(𝑨¯)≤λmax​(𝑲¯)\lambda_{\max}(\bar{\bm{A}})\leq\lambda_{\max}(\bar{\bm{K}}), so even KronLSTM’s fastest-decaying mode is no faster than DeltaNet’s. The comparison is therefore not a trade of some directions against others: the whole spectrum of retention rates moves in KronLSTM’s favour. For isotropic values it moves by exactly the factor 1/d1/d, λk​(𝑨¯)=λk​(𝑲¯)/d\lambda_{k}(\bar{\bm{A}})=\lambda_{k}(\bar{\bm{K}})/d with multiplicity dd each.

  • •

    On average, likewise. Comparing (A145) with (A146) for isotropic values, Tr​𝑴t/d2=1d​∑k(1−β​λk​(𝑲¯)/d)t≥1d​∑k(1−β​λk​(𝑲¯))t=Tr​𝑵t/d\mathbf{\mathrm{Tr}}\bm{M}^{t}/d^{2}=\tfrac{1}{d}\sum_{k}(1-\beta\lambda_{k}(\bar{\bm{K}})/d)^{t}\geq\tfrac{1}{d}\sum_{k}(1-\beta\lambda_{k}(\bar{\bm{K}}))^{t}=\mathbf{\mathrm{Tr}}\bm{N}^{t}/d termwise.

Retention is bought from adaptation.

The same matrix 𝑴t\bm{M}^{t} governs both terms of (A142): the acquired memory approaches 𝒔LS\bm{s}^{\mathrm{L}\mathrm{S}} at rate 𝑰−𝑴t\bm{I}-\bm{M}^{t}. Retaining the initial memory dd times longer therefore means approaching the least-squares memory dd times more slowly, at fixed β\beta. The statement is not that KronLSTM forgets less for free, but that its per-step write is dd times gentler in every direction of an d2d^{2}-dimensional memory, where DeltaNet’s is concentrated on a dd-dimensional one — the same trade-off that appears in the capacity count (d2d^{2} against dd exactly satisfiable associations) and in the norm bound, seen through its time constant. Long contexts are precisely the regime in which the number of associations, not the speed of fitting any one of them, is binding.

Appendix A6 Further Results

A6.1  400M language models

Models with 400M/40B (Table A2) are closer to each other in their performance. KronLSTM has the best average and performs best on HellaSwag, ARC-easy, ARC-challenge, and WinoGrande. Mamba-3 is best on PIQA, KDA on LAMBADA, and GDN-2 on WinoGrande where it ties with KronLSTM. Compared with mLSTM, the matrix-memory xLSTM variant that KronLSTM builds on, KronLSTM is better on five of the six tasks, raises the average by 2.1 points, and lowers LAMBADA perplexity from 43.40 to 28.28. mLSTM is only marginally ahead on PIQA.

A6.2  Ablation on different formulations of KronLSTM

Table A3 ablates the components of the KronLSTM write rule at 1.5B/100B. We report Avg-6, the mean accuracy over the five commonsense reasoning tasks and LAMBADA, together with LAMBADA perplexity, the average over the six-task real-world recall suite at 2k context, and the average over the six RULER NIAH tasks of Table 3 at 4k, 8k and 16k. Three variants are compared with the base model of (10):
(1) the ℓ2\ell_{2}-normalization of 𝒗t\bm{v}_{t} is removed;
(2) erase and write are coupled by using the target ctc_{t} instead of c~t=ct/βt\tilde{c}_{t}=c_{t}/\beta_{t}, so that βt\beta_{t} scales both terms as in Gated DeltaNet;
(3) the write gate is fixed to the unit target ct≡1c_{t}\equiv 1.

On language modeling, variants (1) and (2) stay within 0.3 accuracy points and 0.25 perplexity points of the base model, with the coupled variant marginally ahead on both. Fixing the target costs 1.6 accuracy points and 0.8 perplexity points, the largest degradation among the ablations. On the recall suite, variants (1) and (2) gain 1.0 and 0.5 points, respectively. On NIAH the ordering reverses: at 4k the base model leads the coupled variant by 12.6 points and the unnormalized variant by 19.9 points, at 8k the unnormalized variant is ahead by 2.2 points, and at 16k the base model leads all three variants. The learned write gate and the decoupled write therefore matter most for retrieval within the pretraining context, while their effect on language modeling is small.

A6.3  Long context extension results

Appendix A7 Pretraining Details

All models are pretrained from scratch using lm-engine Mishra (2024) with Triton kernels from flash-linear-attention Yang and Zhang (2026) whenever available. Every mixer in a comparison shares the corpus, the tokenizer, the optimizer, the schedule, the batch size, and the seed; we only change the sequence mixer blocks. The models were trained on 16 nodes of 4×\timesNVIDIA GH200. Training is pure data parallelism under the FSDP-2 with bf16 mixed-precision.

Data and tokenization

We train on the FineWeb-Edu 100BT sample, tokenized with the Llama 2 tokenizer with its standard vocab size of 32,000. Documents are concatenated, separated by the EOS token, and packed into fixed-length sequences of 8192 tokens; This is applied identically to every experiment.

Architecture

All models are decoder-only and identical outside the sequence mixer. We implemented the block structures of every baseline as in the original works. Mamba-3 was trained using the standard expansion factor of 2, a dstate of 128, and a head dimension of 64. For Mamba-3, we utilized the SISO formulation. For the other baselines and our method, we utilized dq​k=dv=128d_{qk}=d_{v}=128. This makes the state size equal across all models. 1.5B models have 2424 layers, a hidden dimension of 20482048 with 16 heads. The 400M models have 24 layers with a hidden dimension of 10241024 and 4 heads (here dv=256d_{v}=256).

Optimization
optimizer AdamW, β=(0.9,0.95)\beta=(0.9,0.95), ϵ=10−10\epsilon=10^{-10}
peak learning rate 3×10−43\times 10^{-4}
schedule linear warmup over 10% of steps, then cosine to 0.1×0.1\times peak (3×10−53\times 10^{-5})
weight decay 0.1, excluding norms, biases, AlogA_{\log}, bΔb_{\Delta} and the gate bias
gradient clipping global norm 1.0
sequence length 8192
global batch 128 sequences == 1,048,576 tokens per step
precision bf16 mixed precision, fp32 optimiser state

A7.1  Long-context extension

The context-extended models of Section 3.3 branch from the 1.5B pretraining runs at 75B tokens and are trained for a further 25B tokens at a sequence length of 32,768, so that both extended models finish at exactly 100B tokens and are token-matched to the 8k-pretrained models. The architecture, tokenizer, and all model hyperparameters are unchanged. The global batch is held at the same 1M tokens per step, now as 32 sequences of 32,768 tokens instead of 128 sequences of 8,192.

Optimization.

The optimizer state is re-initialized at the branch point for both models and the schedule restarts: linear warmup over 5% to a peak learning rate of 8.4×10−58.4\times 10^{-5}, which is the value the parent cosine schedule had reached at the checkpoint, followed by cosine decay over 23,800 steps to 0.1×0.1\times the peak. This mirrors the warmup-and-decay shape used by Gao et al. (2024). AdamW hyperparameters, weight decay, and gradient clipping are as in Appendix A7.

Data.

The corpus takes the four long-document domains of ProLong-64K (Gao et al., 2024), books, code, textbooks, and arXiv, re-tokenized with the Llama 2 tokenizer, and blends them at the ratios of Gao et al. (2024) with FineWeb-Edu in place of their short-context mixture. Documents are concatenated and packed into sequences of 32,768 tokens as in pretraining.

Systems.

Training runs on 8 nodes of 4×4\timesNVIDIA GH200 with ZeRO stage 2 and block-wise gradient checkpointing under bf16 mixed precision.

A7.2  State Tracking Experiments

State-tracking tasks.

Each sample is a token sequence of length ∼𝒰⁡[2,128]\sim\mathcal{U}[2,128] padded to the context length, with a single supervised position at its end. Parity: i.i.d. uniform bits, label the parity of the number of ones (chance 50%50\%). S3S_{3}: i.i.d. uniform transpositions (0 1),(0 2),(1 2)(0\,1),(0\,2),(1\,2), label the prefix product x1∘⋯∘xℓx_{1}\circ\dots\circ x_{\ell} as one of the six group elements (chance 16.7%16.7\%; tracking parity alone gives 33.3%33.3\%). Modular arithmetic: an expression d1​o1​d2​…​dk=d_{1}\,o_{1}\,d_{2}\dots d_{k}\,= with uniform digits in {0,…,4}\{0,\dots,4\} and operators in {+,−,×}\{+,-,\times\}, evaluated with operator precedence modulo 5, the result supervised at the = token (chance 20%20\%). Samples are generated on the fly and deterministically from the run seed (seeds 1-3); evaluation uses 50,00050{,}000 fresh sequences per length L∈{128,256,512,1024}L\in\{128,256,512,1024\}.

Models and training.

All models share a 128-dimensional embedding, pre-norm residual blocks (RMSNorm, no feed-forward sublayer) and a linear read-out; they differ only in the mixer: Gated DeltaNet with the eigenvalue range extended to [−1,1][-1,1] (Grazzi et al., 2025), Mamba-3 (SISO, expansion 2, state size 128, data-dependent RoPE), and KronLSTM. For optimizer we used AdamW with weight decay 0.10.1, batch size 128, bf16. Parity and S3S_{3}: two blocks, constant learning rate ∈{10−3,10−4}\in\{10^{-3},10^{-4}\}, 50k steps, gradient clipping 100. Modular arithmetic requires depth and a longer budget for all three architectures: three blocks, 150k steps. We report end-of-training accuracy, mean ±\pm standard deviation over three seeds, at the learning rate with the best mean accuracy over L∈{256}L\in\{256\}.

Appendix A8 Chunkwise-Parallel Training of KronLSTM

The KronLSTM update (10) revises the matrix memory by a rank-one term whose coefficient depends on the memory only through a scalar. It therefore admits the chunkwise-parallel training scheme of DeltaNet (Yang et al., 2024), Gated DeltaNet (Yang et al., 2025), Kimi Delta Attention (Kimi Team et al., 2025), and Gated DeltaNet-2 (Hatamizadeh et al., 2026): the sequence is split into chunks of length CC, all token interactions inside a chunk are expressed as dense matrix products and one small triangular solve, and the memory is propagated only between chunks. Three points differ from the delta rule. (i) The triangular solve is built on the Gram matrix of the Kronecker features 𝒂t=𝒌t⊗𝒗t\bm{a}_{t}=\bm{k}_{t}\otimes\bm{v}_{t}, which by the mixed-product property is the Hadamard product of a (decay-weighted) key Gram and the value Gram; the dk​dvd_{k}d_{v}-dimensional features are never formed. (ii) The pseudo-values are scalar multiples ur​𝒗ru_{r}\bm{v}_{r} of the values. (iii) The incoming memory of a chunk enters the solve through CC scalar scores 𝒗r⊤​𝑺0​(𝜸r⊙𝒌r)\bm{v}_{r}^{\top}\bm{S}_{0}(\bm{\gamma}_{r}\odot\bm{k}_{r}) instead of the dvd_{v}-dimensional read-outs 𝑺0​𝒌r\bm{S}_{0}\bm{k}_{r} of the delta rule. The vector forget gate is handled as in KDA and Gated DeltaNet-2 by absorbing the cumulative decay into an asymmetric pair of keys.

A8.1  Setting and notation

We consider one chunk of CC tokens and suppress the chunk index. Let 𝑺0∈ℝdv×dk\bm{S}_{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{v}\times d_{k}} be the memory entering the chunk and let 𝒒r,𝒌r∈ℝdk\bm{q}_{r},\bm{k}_{r}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{k}}, 𝒗r∈ℝdv\bm{v}_{r}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{v}}, βr,cr∈ℝ\beta_{r},c_{r}\in\mathbb{R} and 𝐟r∈(0,1)dk\mathbf{f}_{r}\in(0,1)^{d_{k}}, 𝑭r=diag⁡(𝐟r)\bm{F}_{r}=\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf{f}_{r}), be the inputs and gates of the rr-th token, r=1,…,Cr=1,\dots,C. Writing 𝑺r\bm{S}_{r} for the memory after token rr, the update (10) and the read-out are11 1 This is (10) with the time index shifted by one, so that 𝑺r\bm{S}_{r} denotes the memory after the write of token rr. The read-out uses this memory, 𝒉r=𝑺r​𝒒r\bm{h}_{r}=\bm{S}_{r}\bm{q}_{r}, i.e., the query of token rr sees the association written at token rr, as in DeltaNet and its gated variants and in our kernels.

𝑺r=𝑺r−1​𝑭r+ur​𝒗r​𝒌r⊤,ur:=cr−βr​yr,yr:=𝒗r⊤​𝑺r−1​𝑭r​𝒌r,𝒉r=𝑺r​𝒒r.\bm{S}_{r}\;=\;\bm{S}_{r-1}\bm{F}_{r}\;+\;u_{r}\,\bm{v}_{r}\bm{k}_{r}^{\top},\qquad u_{r}\;:=\;c_{r}-\beta_{r}\,y_{r},\qquad y_{r}\;:=\;\bm{v}_{r}^{\top}\,\bm{S}_{r-1}\bm{F}_{r}\,\bm{k}_{r},\qquad\bm{h}_{r}\;=\;\bm{S}_{r}\bm{q}_{r}. (A149)

We call yry_{r} the score of the pair (𝒌r,𝒗r)(\bm{k}_{r},\bm{v}_{r}) on the decayed memory and uru_{r} the write coefficient, the coefficient of the rank-one write along 𝒗r​𝒌r⊤\bm{v}_{r}\bm{k}_{r}^{\top}. It is the only quantity in (A149) that depends on the memory.

Cumulative decay.

With ℓr:=∑i≤rlog⁡𝐟i\bm{\ell}_{r}:=\sum_{i\leq r}\log\mathbf{f}_{i} (a cumulative sum inside the chunk) we set

𝜸r:=exp(ℓr)=𝐟1⊙⋯⊙𝐟r∈(0,1]dk,𝜸0:= 1,𝚪r:=diag(𝜸r)=𝑭1⋯𝑭r.\bm{\gamma}_{r}\;:=\;\exp(\bm{\ell}_{r})\;=\;\mathbf{f}_{1}\odot\cdots\odot\mathbf{f}_{r}\;\in\;(0,1]^{d_{k}},\qquad\bm{\gamma}_{0}\;:=\;\bm{1},\qquad\bm{\Gamma}_{r}\;:=\;\operatorname{diag}(\bm{\gamma}_{r})\;=\;\bm{F}_{1}\cdots\bm{F}_{r}. (A150)

All products, quotients and exponentials of 𝜸\bm{\gamma}’s are element-wise over the key dimension. For s≤rs\leq r the ratio 𝜸r/𝜸s=𝐟s+1⊙⋯⊙𝐟r\bm{\gamma}_{r}/\bm{\gamma}_{s}=\mathbf{f}_{s+1}\odot\cdots\odot\mathbf{f}_{r} lies in (0,1]dk(0,1]^{d_{k}}; it is the decay that a key written at token ss has undergone by token rr. Four decay-scaled copies of the keys and queries appear:

𝒌^r:=𝜸r⊙𝒌r,𝒌¯r:=𝒌r/𝜸r,𝒌˘r:=(𝜸C/𝜸r)⊙𝒌r,𝒒^r:=𝜸r⊙𝒒r.\widehat{\bm{k}}_{r}\;:=\;\bm{\gamma}_{r}\odot\bm{k}_{r},\qquad\bar{\bm{k}}_{r}\;:=\;\bm{k}_{r}/\bm{\gamma}_{r},\qquad\breve{\bm{k}}_{r}\;:=\;(\bm{\gamma}_{C}/\bm{\gamma}_{r})\odot\bm{k}_{r},\qquad\widehat{\bm{q}}_{r}\;:=\;\bm{\gamma}_{r}\odot\bm{q}_{r}. (A151)

𝒌^r\widehat{\bm{k}}_{r} is the key with which the memory is scored, 𝒌¯r\bar{\bm{k}}_{r} the key along which it is written in the decay-normalized frame of Section A8.2, and 𝒌˘r\breve{\bm{k}}_{r} the key as it appears in the memory at the end of the chunk.

Stacked matrices.

𝑲,𝑸∈ℝC×dk\bm{K},\bm{Q}\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times d_{k}} and 𝑽∈ℝC×dv\bm{V}\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times d_{v}} stack 𝒌r⊤\bm{k}_{r}^{\top}, 𝒒r⊤\bm{q}_{r}^{\top}, 𝒗r⊤\bm{v}_{r}^{\top} as rows; 𝑲^,𝑲¯,𝑲˘,𝑸^\widehat{\bm{K}},\bar{\bm{K}},\breve{\bm{K}},\widehat{\bm{Q}} stack the vectors of (A151); 𝜷,𝒄,𝒖,𝒑∈ℝC\bm{\beta},\bm{c},\bm{u},\bm{p}\in\mathbb{R}^{C} stack the scalars; 𝑯∈ℝC×dv\bm{H}\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times d_{v}} stacks the read-outs 𝒉r⊤\bm{h}_{r}^{\top}. The three C×CC\times C matrices

𝑮r​sk​k:= 1[r>s]𝒌^r⊤𝒌¯s= 1[r>s]∑d=1dkkr​dks​dγr​dγs​d,𝑮v​v:=𝑽𝑽⊤,𝑮r​sq​k:= 1[r≥s]𝒒^r⊤𝒌¯s\bm{G}^{kk}_{rs}\;:=\;\mathbbm{1}[r>s]\;\widehat{\bm{k}}_{r}^{\top}\bar{\bm{k}}_{s}\;=\;\mathbbm{1}[r>s]\sum_{d=1}^{d_{k}}k_{rd}\,k_{sd}\,\frac{\gamma_{rd}}{\gamma_{sd}},\qquad\bm{G}^{vv}\;:=\;\bm{V}\bm{V}^{\top},\qquad\bm{G}^{qk}_{rs}\;:=\;\mathbbm{1}[r\geq s]\;\widehat{\bm{q}}_{r}^{\top}\bar{\bm{k}}_{s} (A152)

are the decay-weighted key Gram (strictly lower triangular), the value Gram, and the decay-weighted read-out Gram (lower triangular with diagonal). All entries of 𝑮k​k\bm{G}^{kk} and 𝑮q​k\bm{G}^{qk} involve only ratios 𝜸r/𝜸s\bm{\gamma}_{r}/\bm{\gamma}_{s} with s≤rs\leq r, hence only factors in (0,1](0,1].

A8.2  Decay-normalized recurrence

The forget gate acts on the key dimension by a diagonal matrix, and diagonal matrices commute. This allows the cumulative decay to be taken out of the recurrence.

Proposition A4 (Decay-normalized recurrence).

Let 𝐒^r:=𝐒r​𝚪r−1\widehat{\bm{S}}_{r}:=\bm{S}_{r}\bm{\Gamma}_{r}^{-1}, so that 𝐒^0=𝐒0\widehat{\bm{S}}_{0}=\bm{S}_{0}. Then, for r=1,…,Cr=1,\dots,C,

𝑺^r=𝑺^r−1+ur​𝒗r​𝒌¯r⊤,yr=𝒗r⊤​𝑺^r−1​𝒌^r,\widehat{\bm{S}}_{r}\;=\;\widehat{\bm{S}}_{r-1}\;+\;u_{r}\,\bm{v}_{r}\bar{\bm{k}}_{r}^{\top},\qquad y_{r}\;=\;\bm{v}_{r}^{\top}\,\widehat{\bm{S}}_{r-1}\,\widehat{\bm{k}}_{r}, (A153)

and consequently

𝑺^r=𝑺0+∑s≤rus​𝒗s​𝒌¯s⊤.\widehat{\bm{S}}_{r}\;=\;\bm{S}_{0}\;+\;\sum_{s\leq r}u_{s}\,\bm{v}_{s}\bar{\bm{k}}_{s}^{\top}. (A154)
Proof.

Since 𝚪r=𝚪r−1​𝑭r\bm{\Gamma}_{r}=\bm{\Gamma}_{r-1}\bm{F}_{r}, we have 𝑺r−1​𝑭r=𝑺^r−1​𝚪r−1​𝑭r=𝑺^r−1​𝚪r\bm{S}_{r-1}\bm{F}_{r}=\widehat{\bm{S}}_{r-1}\bm{\Gamma}_{r-1}\bm{F}_{r}=\widehat{\bm{S}}_{r-1}\bm{\Gamma}_{r}. Inserting this into (A149) gives 𝑺r=𝑺^r−1​𝚪r+ur​𝒗r​𝒌r⊤\bm{S}_{r}=\widehat{\bm{S}}_{r-1}\bm{\Gamma}_{r}+u_{r}\bm{v}_{r}\bm{k}_{r}^{\top}; right-multiplication by 𝚪r−1\bm{\Gamma}_{r}^{-1} yields the first identity, because 𝒌r⊤​𝚪r−1=𝒌¯r⊤\bm{k}_{r}^{\top}\bm{\Gamma}_{r}^{-1}=\bar{\bm{k}}_{r}^{\top}. The second identity is yr=𝒗r⊤​(𝑺^r−1​𝚪r)​𝒌r=𝒗r⊤​𝑺^r−1​(𝚪r​𝒌r)y_{r}=\bm{v}_{r}^{\top}(\widehat{\bm{S}}_{r-1}\bm{\Gamma}_{r})\bm{k}_{r}=\bm{v}_{r}^{\top}\widehat{\bm{S}}_{r-1}(\bm{\Gamma}_{r}\bm{k}_{r}). Unrolling the first identity from 𝑺^0=𝑺0\widehat{\bm{S}}_{0}=\bm{S}_{0} gives (A154). ∎

In the normalized frame the recurrence is the Kronecker Delta Rule without forget gate, applied to an asymmetric key pair: the association is scored with the decayed key 𝒌^r\widehat{\bm{k}}_{r} and written along the un-decayed key 𝒌¯r\bar{\bm{k}}_{r}. This is the same device by which Gated DeltaNet-2 absorbs its channel-wise decay into asymmetric erase factors (Hatamizadeh et al., 2026). Equation (A154) is the additive representation of the memory, 𝑺r=(𝑺0+∑s≤rus​𝒗s​𝒌¯s⊤)​𝚪r\bm{S}_{r}=\big(\bm{S}_{0}+\sum_{s\leq r}u_{s}\bm{v}_{s}\bar{\bm{k}}_{s}^{\top}\big)\bm{\Gamma}_{r}; the memory revisions do not have to be materialized, only the CC scalars usu_{s}.

A8.3  The write coefficients solve a unit lower triangular system

Proposition A5 (Write coefficients).

Let pr:=𝐯r⊤​𝐒0​𝐤^rp_{r}:=\bm{v}_{r}^{\top}\bm{S}_{0}\,\widehat{\bm{k}}_{r} be the score of the rr-th pair on the incoming memory, and let

𝑵:=diag⁡(𝜷)​(𝑮k​k⊙𝑮v​v)∈ℝC×C,𝚲:=(𝑰+𝑵)−1.\bm{N}\;:=\;\operatorname{diag}(\bm{\beta})\,\big(\bm{G}^{kk}\odot\bm{G}^{vv}\big)\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{C\times C},\qquad\bm{\Lambda}\;:=\;(\bm{I}+\bm{N})^{-1}. (A155)

𝑵\bm{N} is strictly lower triangular, so 𝐈+𝐍\bm{I}+\bm{N} is unit lower triangular and invertible for every 𝛃\bm{\beta} and every input. The write coefficients are

𝒖=𝚲(𝒄−𝜷⊙𝒑)=𝚲​𝒄⏟=:𝒖∘−𝚲diag(𝜷)𝒑.\bm{u}\;=\;\bm{\Lambda}\,\big(\bm{c}-\bm{\beta}\odot\bm{p}\big)\;=\;\underbrace{\bm{\Lambda}\,\bm{c}}_{=:\,\bm{u}^{\circ}}\;-\;\bm{\Lambda}\operatorname{diag}(\bm{\beta})\,\bm{p}. (A156)
Proof.

Insert (A154) at r−1r-1 into the score in (A153):

yr=𝒗r⊤​𝑺0​𝒌^r+∑s<rus​(𝒗r⊤​𝒗s)​(𝒌¯s⊤​𝒌^r)=pr+∑s<r(𝑮k​k⊙𝑮v​v)r​s​us.y_{r}\;=\;\bm{v}_{r}^{\top}\bm{S}_{0}\widehat{\bm{k}}_{r}\;+\;\sum_{s<r}u_{s}\,(\bm{v}_{r}^{\top}\bm{v}_{s})(\bar{\bm{k}}_{s}^{\top}\widehat{\bm{k}}_{r})\;=\;p_{r}\;+\;\sum_{s<r}\big(\bm{G}^{kk}\odot\bm{G}^{vv}\big)_{rs}\,u_{s}.

Hence ur=cr−βr​yru_{r}=c_{r}-\beta_{r}y_{r} reads ur+∑s<r𝑵r​s​us=cr−βr​pru_{r}+\sum_{s<r}\bm{N}_{rs}u_{s}=c_{r}-\beta_{r}p_{r}, which is row rr of (𝑰+𝑵)​𝒖=𝒄−𝜷⊙𝒑(\bm{I}+\bm{N})\bm{u}=\bm{c}-\bm{\beta}\odot\bm{p}. ∎

The Gram of the Kronecker features.

With 𝒂^r:=𝒌^r⊗𝒗r\widehat{\bm{a}}_{r}:=\widehat{\bm{k}}_{r}\otimes\bm{v}_{r} and 𝒂¯s:=𝒌¯s⊗𝒗s\bar{\bm{a}}_{s}:=\bar{\bm{k}}_{s}\otimes\bm{v}_{s}, the mixed-product property of the Kronecker product gives 𝒂^r⊤​𝒂¯s=(𝒌^r⊤​𝒌¯s)​(𝒗r⊤​𝒗s)\widehat{\bm{a}}_{r}^{\top}\bar{\bm{a}}_{s}=(\widehat{\bm{k}}_{r}^{\top}\bar{\bm{k}}_{s})(\bm{v}_{r}^{\top}\bm{v}_{s}), so 𝑮k​k⊙𝑮v​v\bm{G}^{kk}\odot\bm{G}^{vv} is the strictly lower triangular part of the Gram matrix of the decay-weighted Kronecker features. Without forget gate (𝐟r≡𝟏\mathbf{f}_{r}\equiv\bm{1}) it is the strictly lower part of the Gram matrix (𝒂r⊤​𝒂s)r​s(\bm{a}_{r}^{\top}\bm{a}_{s})_{rs} of the features 𝒂r=𝒌r⊗𝒗r\bm{a}_{r}=\bm{k}_{r}\otimes\bm{v}_{r}, i.e., exactly the matrix that the UT transform of DeltaNet (Yang et al., 2024) builds from 𝑲​𝑲⊤\bm{K}\bm{K}^{\top}, with the feature 𝒂r\bm{a}_{r} in place of 𝒌r\bm{k}_{r} as anticipated by the vectorized form (4). The dk​dvd_{k}d_{v}-dimensional features are never formed: two C×CC\times C Gram matrices of dkd_{k}- and dvd_{v}-dimensional vectors and one Hadamard product suffice.

Decoupled erase and write.

The write gate crc_{r} enters only the right-hand side of the solve, the erase gate βr\beta_{r} enters the system matrix and the coupling to 𝑺0\bm{S}_{0}. The state-independent part 𝒖∘=𝚲​𝒄\bm{u}^{\circ}=\bm{\Lambda}\bm{c} and the matrix 𝚲​diag⁡(𝜷)\bm{\Lambda}\operatorname{diag}(\bm{\beta}) can be computed for all chunks in parallel; they are the analogues of the pseudo-values 𝑼=𝑻​𝑽\bm{U}=\bm{T}\bm{V} and of 𝑾=𝑻​𝑲\bm{W}=\bm{T}\bm{K} in DeltaNet. The only sequential quantity is the vector of scores 𝒑\bm{p}.

A8.4  Chunkwise form

Theorem A11 (Chunkwise KronLSTM).

Let 𝐕~:=diag⁡(𝐮)​𝐕∈ℝC×dv\widetilde{\bm{V}}:=\operatorname{diag}(\bm{u})\,\bm{V}\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times d_{v}} be the matrix of pseudo-values, with rows ur​𝐯r⊤u_{r}\bm{v}_{r}^{\top}, where 𝐮\bm{u} is given by Proposition A5 and

𝒑=((𝑽​𝑺0)⊙𝑲^)​ 1(row sums of a C×dk matrix).\bm{p}\;=\;\big((\bm{V}\bm{S}_{0})\odot\widehat{\bm{K}}\big)\,\bm{1}\qquad\text{(row sums of a $C\times d_{k}$ matrix).} (A157)

Then the memory at the end of the chunk and the read-outs of the chunk are

𝑺C\displaystyle\bm{S}_{C} =𝑺0​𝚪C+𝑽~⊤​𝑲˘∈ℝdv×dk,\displaystyle\;=\;\bm{S}_{0}\,\bm{\Gamma}_{C}\;+\;\widetilde{\bm{V}}^{\top}\breve{\bm{K}}\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{d_{v}\times d_{k}}, (A158)
𝑯\displaystyle\bm{H} =𝑸^​𝑺0⊤+𝑮q​k​𝑽~∈ℝC×dv.\displaystyle\;=\;\widehat{\bm{Q}}\,\bm{S}_{0}^{\top}\;+\;\bm{G}^{qk}\,\widetilde{\bm{V}}\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{C\times d_{v}}. (A159)
Proof.

Equation (A157) is pr=𝒗r⊤​𝑺0​𝒌^r=∑d(𝑽​𝑺0)r​d​K^r​dp_{r}=\bm{v}_{r}^{\top}\bm{S}_{0}\widehat{\bm{k}}_{r}=\sum_{d}(\bm{V}\bm{S}_{0})_{rd}\,\widehat{K}_{rd}. For the state, 𝑺C=𝑺^C​𝚪C=𝑺0​𝚪C+∑s≤Cus​𝒗s​𝒌¯s⊤​𝚪C\bm{S}_{C}=\widehat{\bm{S}}_{C}\bm{\Gamma}_{C}=\bm{S}_{0}\bm{\Gamma}_{C}+\sum_{s\leq C}u_{s}\bm{v}_{s}\bar{\bm{k}}_{s}^{\top}\bm{\Gamma}_{C} by (A154), and 𝒌¯s⊤​𝚪C=((𝜸C/𝜸s)⊙𝒌s)⊤=𝒌˘s⊤\bar{\bm{k}}_{s}^{\top}\bm{\Gamma}_{C}=\big((\bm{\gamma}_{C}/\bm{\gamma}_{s})\odot\bm{k}_{s}\big)^{\top}=\breve{\bm{k}}_{s}^{\top}, which is (A158). For the read-out, 𝒉r=𝑺r​𝒒r=𝑺^r​𝚪r​𝒒r=𝑺^r​𝒒^r=𝑺0​𝒒^r+∑s≤rus​(𝒌¯s⊤​𝒒^r)​𝒗s\bm{h}_{r}=\bm{S}_{r}\bm{q}_{r}=\widehat{\bm{S}}_{r}\bm{\Gamma}_{r}\bm{q}_{r}=\widehat{\bm{S}}_{r}\widehat{\bm{q}}_{r}=\bm{S}_{0}\widehat{\bm{q}}_{r}+\sum_{s\leq r}u_{s}\,(\bar{\bm{k}}_{s}^{\top}\widehat{\bm{q}}_{r})\,\bm{v}_{s} by (A154); transposing and stacking over rr gives (A159), the coefficient of us​𝒗s⊤u_{s}\bm{v}_{s}^{\top} in row rr being 𝑮r​sq​k\bm{G}^{qk}_{rs}. ∎

Indexing the chunks by [n][n] and writing 𝑺[n]\bm{S}_{[n]} for the memory entering chunk nn, (A158) is the chunk-level recurrence

𝑺[n+1]=𝑺[n]​𝚪[n],C+𝑽~[n]⊤​𝑲˘[n],\bm{S}_{[n+1]}\;=\;\bm{S}_{[n]}\,\bm{\Gamma}_{[n],C}\;+\;\widetilde{\bm{V}}_{[n]}^{\top}\breve{\bm{K}}_{[n]}, (A160)

with 𝑺[0]=𝟎\bm{S}_{[0]}=\bm{0} (or a given initial memory). Everything in (A152)–(A159) except 𝒑\bm{p}, 𝒖\bm{u} and 𝑽~\widetilde{\bm{V}} is local to a chunk and is computed for all chunks at once; the dependence 𝑺[n]→𝒑→𝒖→𝑺[n+1]\bm{S}_{[n]}\to\bm{p}\to\bm{u}\to\bm{S}_{[n+1]} is the only sequential part. Compared with the delta-rule family, the pseudo-value of token rr is the value 𝒗r\bm{v}_{r} scaled by the scalar uru_{r}, and the memory couples into the chunk through the CC scalars 𝒑\bm{p} rather than through the CC vectors 𝑺0​𝒌r∈ℝdv\bm{S}_{0}\bm{k}_{r}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{v}}: computing 𝒑\bm{p} needs one matrix product 𝑽​𝑺0\bm{V}\bm{S}_{0} and a row-wise contraction over the value dimension, which is where a kernel that tiles the memory over dvd_{v} must exchange partial sums.

A8.5  WY representation of the chunk transition

In vectorized form, 𝒔=vec⁡(𝑺)\bm{s}=\vecop(\bm{S}) with vec⁡(𝒗​𝒌⊤)=𝒌⊗𝒗\vecop(\bm{v}\bm{k}^{\top})=\bm{k}\otimes\bm{v} and vec⁡(𝑺​𝑭)=(𝑭⊗𝑰dv)​vec⁡(𝑺)\vecop(\bm{S}\bm{F})=(\bm{F}\otimes\bm{I}_{d_{v}})\vecop(\bm{S}), one step of (A149) is 𝒔r=(𝑰−βr​𝒂r​𝒂r⊤)​(𝑭r⊗𝑰dv)​𝒔r−1+cr​𝒂r\bm{s}_{r}=(\bm{I}-\beta_{r}\bm{a}_{r}\bm{a}_{r}^{\top})(\bm{F}_{r}\otimes\bm{I}_{d_{v}})\,\bm{s}_{r-1}+c_{r}\bm{a}_{r} with 𝒂r=𝒌r⊗𝒗r\bm{a}_{r}=\bm{k}_{r}\otimes\bm{v}_{r}: a generalized Householder transition, as in (4), preceded by a diagonal decay. Theorem A11 is the WY representation (Bischof and VanLoan, 1987) of the product of these factors.

Corollary A7 (WY form).

Let 𝐀^:=[𝐤^1⊗𝐯1,…,𝐤^C⊗𝐯C]\widehat{\bm{A}}:=[\widehat{\bm{k}}_{1}\otimes\bm{v}_{1},\dots,\widehat{\bm{k}}_{C}\otimes\bm{v}_{C}] and 𝐀˘:=[𝐤˘1⊗𝐯1,…,𝐤˘C⊗𝐯C]\breve{\bm{A}}:=[\breve{\bm{k}}_{1}\otimes\bm{v}_{1},\dots,\breve{\bm{k}}_{C}\otimes\bm{v}_{C}] in ℝdk​dv×C\mathbb{R}^{d_{k}d_{v}\times C}. Then 𝐬C=𝐏​𝐬0+𝐝\bm{s}_{C}=\bm{P}\,\bm{s}_{0}+\bm{d} with

𝑷=∏r=C1(𝑰−βr​𝒂r​𝒂r⊤)​(𝑭r⊗𝑰dv)=(𝚪C⊗𝑰dv)−𝑨˘​𝚲​diag⁡(𝜷)​𝑨^⊤,𝒅=𝑨˘​𝚲​𝒄.\bm{P}\;=\;\prod_{r=C}^{1}(\bm{I}-\beta_{r}\bm{a}_{r}\bm{a}_{r}^{\top})(\bm{F}_{r}\otimes\bm{I}_{d_{v}})\;=\;(\bm{\Gamma}_{C}\otimes\bm{I}_{d_{v}})\;-\;\breve{\bm{A}}\,\bm{\Lambda}\operatorname{diag}(\bm{\beta})\,\widehat{\bm{A}}^{\top},\qquad\bm{d}\;=\;\breve{\bm{A}}\,\bm{\Lambda}\,\bm{c}. (A161)
Proof.

By (A158), 𝒔C=(𝚪C⊗𝑰)​𝒔0+∑rur​(𝒌˘r⊗𝒗r)=(𝚪C⊗𝑰)​𝒔0+𝑨˘​𝒖\bm{s}_{C}=(\bm{\Gamma}_{C}\otimes\bm{I})\bm{s}_{0}+\sum_{r}u_{r}(\breve{\bm{k}}_{r}\otimes\bm{v}_{r})=(\bm{\Gamma}_{C}\otimes\bm{I})\bm{s}_{0}+\breve{\bm{A}}\bm{u}. Since pr=⟨𝒗r​𝒌^r⊤,𝑺0⟩F=𝒂^r⊤​𝒔0p_{r}=\langle\bm{v}_{r}\widehat{\bm{k}}_{r}^{\top},\bm{S}_{0}\rangle_{F}=\widehat{\bm{a}}_{r}^{\top}\bm{s}_{0}, we have 𝒑=𝑨^⊤​𝒔0\bm{p}=\widehat{\bm{A}}^{\top}\bm{s}_{0}, and (A156) gives 𝒖=𝚲​𝒄−𝚲​diag⁡(𝜷)​𝑨^⊤​𝒔0\bm{u}=\bm{\Lambda}\bm{c}-\bm{\Lambda}\operatorname{diag}(\bm{\beta})\widehat{\bm{A}}^{\top}\bm{s}_{0}. ∎

The correction to the diagonal decay has rank at most CC, as for DeltaNet, where 𝑷=𝑰−∑s𝒘s​𝒌s⊤\bm{P}=\bm{I}-\sum_{s}\bm{w}_{s}\bm{k}_{s}^{\top}. The difference is that the columns of 𝑨˘​𝚲​diag⁡(𝜷)\breve{\bm{A}}\bm{\Lambda}\operatorname{diag}(\bm{\beta}) are linear combinations of Kronecker products 𝒌˘s⊗𝒗s\breve{\bm{k}}_{s}\otimes\bm{v}_{s} and are in general not themselves Kronecker products, so the correction is not of the delta-rule form ∑s(𝑺0​𝒘s)​𝒌s⊤\sum_{s}(\bm{S}_{0}\bm{w}_{s})\bm{k}_{s}^{\top}, in which the memory enters through the dvd_{v}-dimensional read-outs 𝑺0​𝒘s\bm{S}_{0}\bm{w}_{s}. Instead the memory enters through the CC scalars 𝒑\bm{p}, and each pseudo-value is 𝒗s\bm{v}_{s} scaled by a linear functional of 𝑺0\bm{S}_{0}. Table A5 summarizes the roles of the chunk quantities in the delta-rule family and in KronLSTM.

A8.6  Variants

The derivation uses only the structure “diagonal decay on the key side, rank-one write along 𝒗r​𝒌r⊤\bm{v}_{r}\bm{k}_{r}^{\top} with a coefficient affine in the scalar score”:

  • •

    Coupled erase and write (variant “β\beta on both sides” of Table A3; target crc_{r} instead of c~r=cr/βr\tilde{c}_{r}=c_{r}/\beta_{r}): replace 𝒄\bm{c} by 𝜷⊙𝒄\bm{\beta}\odot\bm{c} in (A156). Unit target (variant “non-learnable target”): 𝒄=𝟏\bm{c}=\bm{1}, so 𝒖∘=𝚲​𝟏\bm{u}^{\circ}=\bm{\Lambda}\bm{1}.

  • •

    State tracking, βr∈(0,2)\beta_{r}\in(0,2) (Section 3.4): nothing changes. 𝑰+𝑵\bm{I}+\bm{N} is unit lower triangular for every 𝜷\bm{\beta}, so the solve needs no condition on the gates or on the data.

  • •

    Scalar forget gate 𝐟r=fr​𝟏\mathbf{f}_{r}=f_{r}\bm{1} (as in Gated DeltaNet): 𝜸r\bm{\gamma}_{r} is a scalar and 𝑮r​sk​k=𝟙[r>s](𝒌r⊤𝒌s)γr/γs\bm{G}^{kk}_{rs}=\mathbbm{1}[{r>s}]\,(\bm{k}_{r}^{\top}\bm{k}_{s})\,\gamma_{r}/\gamma_{s}. No forget gate: 𝑮k​k=stril⁡(𝑲​𝑲⊤)\bm{G}^{kk}=\operatorname{stril}(\bm{K}\bm{K}^{\top}) and 𝑲˘=𝑲^=𝑲¯=𝑲\breve{\bm{K}}=\widehat{\bm{K}}=\bar{\bm{K}}=\bm{K}.

  • •

    Values of arbitrary norm. The kernels accept unnormalized values by the substitution βr←βr/‖𝒗r‖2\beta_{r}\leftarrow\beta_{r}/\left\lVert\bm{v}_{r}\right\rVert^{2} (the erase step is capped so that βr​‖𝒂r‖2=βr\beta_{r}\left\lVert\bm{a}_{r}\right\rVert^{2}=\beta_{r} for unit-norm keys and the contraction condition of Property A6 holds independently of ‖𝒗r‖\left\lVert\bm{v}_{r}\right\rVert); the write gate is unaffected. With the ℓ2\ell_{2}-normalized values of Section 2.2 this is (A149).

A8.7  Algorithm, cost and implementation

Algorithm (forward pass, one head).

Given 𝑸,𝑲∈ℝL×dk\bm{Q},\bm{K}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{k}}, 𝑽∈ℝL×dv\bm{V}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{v}}, 𝜷,𝒄∈ℝL\bm{\beta},\bm{c}\in\mathbb{R}^{L}, log⁡𝐟∈ℝL×dk\log\mathbf{f}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{k}}, a chunk length CC and an initial memory 𝑺[0]\bm{S}_{[0]}:

  1. 1.

    Chunk-local, in parallel over chunks. For every chunk: ℓ←cumsum⁡(log⁡𝐟)\bm{\ell}\leftarrow\operatorname{cumsum}(\log\mathbf{f}) within the chunk, 𝜸←exp⁡(ℓ)\bm{\gamma}\leftarrow\exp(\bm{\ell}), and 𝑲^,𝑲¯,𝑲˘,𝑸^\widehat{\bm{K}},\bar{\bm{K}},\breve{\bm{K}},\widehat{\bm{Q}} as in (A151); 𝑮k​k,𝑮v​v,𝑮q​k\bm{G}^{kk},\bm{G}^{vv},\bm{G}^{qk} as in (A152), the entries of 𝑮k​k\bm{G}^{kk} and 𝑮q​k\bm{G}^{qk} via exp⁡(ℓr−ℓs)\exp(\bm{\ell}_{r}-\bm{\ell}_{s}) for s≤rs\leq r; 𝑵←diag⁡(𝜷)​(𝑮k​k⊙𝑮v​v)\bm{N}\leftarrow\operatorname{diag}(\bm{\beta})(\bm{G}^{kk}\odot\bm{G}^{vv}) and 𝚲←(𝑰+𝑵)−1\bm{\Lambda}\leftarrow(\bm{I}+\bm{N})^{-1} by forward substitution; 𝒖∘←𝚲​𝒄\bm{u}^{\circ}\leftarrow\bm{\Lambda}\bm{c} and 𝚲β←𝚲​diag⁡(𝜷)\bm{\Lambda}_{\beta}\leftarrow\bm{\Lambda}\operatorname{diag}(\bm{\beta}).

  2. 2.

    Scan, sequential over chunks. 𝑺←𝑺[0]\bm{S}\leftarrow\bm{S}_{[0]}; for n=0,1,…n=0,1,\dots: 𝒑←((𝑽​𝑺)⊙𝑲^)​𝟏\bm{p}\leftarrow\big((\bm{V}\bm{S})\odot\widehat{\bm{K}}\big)\bm{1}; 𝒖←𝒖∘−𝚲β​𝒑\bm{u}\leftarrow\bm{u}^{\circ}-\bm{\Lambda}_{\beta}\,\bm{p}; 𝑽~←diag⁡(𝒖)​𝑽\widetilde{\bm{V}}\leftarrow\operatorname{diag}(\bm{u})\bm{V}; 𝑯[n]←𝑸^​𝑺⊤+𝑮q​k​𝑽~\bm{H}_{[n]}\leftarrow\widehat{\bm{Q}}\bm{S}^{\top}+\bm{G}^{qk}\widetilde{\bm{V}}; 𝑺←𝑺​diag⁡(𝜸C)+𝑽~⊤​𝑲˘\bm{S}\leftarrow\bm{S}\operatorname{diag}(\bm{\gamma}_{C})+\widetilde{\bm{V}}^{\top}\breve{\bm{K}}.

  3. 3.

    Return 𝑯∈ℝL×dv\bm{H}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times d_{v}} and the final memory 𝑺\bm{S}.

Cost.

Per chunk and head the algorithm performs the two C×CC\times C key Grams (2​C2​dk2C^{2}d_{k} multiply–adds), the value Gram (C2​dvC^{2}d_{v}), one unit lower triangular solve applied to two right-hand sides (O⁡(C3)O(C^{3}), in practice on 16×1616\times 16 blocks as in the delta-rule kernels), three products with the memory, 𝑽​𝑺\bm{V}\bm{S}, 𝑸^​𝑺⊤\widehat{\bm{Q}}\bm{S}^{\top} and 𝑽~⊤​𝑲˘\widetilde{\bm{V}}^{\top}\breve{\bm{K}} (3​C​dk​dv3Cd_{k}d_{v}), and the intra-chunk product 𝑮q​k​𝑽~\bm{G}^{qk}\widetilde{\bm{V}} (C2​dvC^{2}d_{v}). Over a sequence of length LL this is O⁡(L​C​(dk+dv)+L​dk​dv)O\big(LC(d_{k}+d_{v})+Ld_{k}d_{v}\big) multiply–adds and O⁡(L​C2)O(LC^{2}) for the solves, the same order as Gated DeltaNet and KDA; relative to KDA the additional cost is the value Gram 𝑮v​v\bm{G}^{vv}, and the coupling 𝒑\bm{p} replaces the product 𝑾​𝑺0\bm{W}\bm{S}_{0} of the delta rule at equal cost. The memory is materialized once per chunk, not per token.

Implementation notes.

(i) The cumulative decays are kept in log space; the Gram entries use exp⁡(ℓr−ℓs)\exp(\bm{\ell}_{r}-\bm{\ell}_{s}) for s≤rs\leq r only, so all decay factors lie in (0,1](0,1] and no quotient 1/𝜸1/\bm{\gamma} is ever formed (the kernels use base-2 logarithms and exp2\exp_{2}). (ii) The triangular solve is the precision-sensitive step and is carried out in IEEE fp32; the remaining products run on tensor cores. (iii) In the fused kernel the solve is not materialized as 𝒖∘\bm{u}^{\circ} and 𝚲β\bm{\Lambda}_{\beta} but applied inside the scan as 𝒖=𝚲⁡(𝒄−𝜷⊙𝒑)\bm{u}=\bm{\Lambda}(\bm{c}-\bm{\beta}\odot\bm{p}). (iv) Because 𝒑\bm{p} contracts over the full value dimension, programs that tile the memory over dvd_{v} exchange their partial row sums of (𝑽​𝑺)⊙𝑲^(\bm{V}\bm{S})\odot\widehat{\bm{K}} once per chunk; this is a synchronization, not a bandwidth cost (CC floats per program against a dk×dvd_{k}\times d_{v} memory). (v) Padding a sequence to a multiple of CC with zero 𝒒,𝒌,𝒗\bm{q},\bm{k},\bm{v}, β=c=0\beta=c=0 and log⁡𝐟=𝟎\log\mathbf{f}=\bm{0} neither writes nor decays. (vi) Queries are scaled by dk−1/2d_{k}^{-1/2} inside the kernel; the scale is immaterial after the RMSNorm of the block. In the supplied code, 𝑲^,𝑲¯,𝑲˘,𝑸^\widehat{\bm{K}},\bar{\bm{K}},\breve{\bm{K}},\widehat{\bm{Q}} are k_up, k_dn, k_tail, q_up; 𝑮k​k,𝑮v​v,𝑮q​k\bm{G}^{kk},\bm{G}^{vv},\bm{G}^{qk} are A_kk, A_vv, A_qk; 𝚲\bm{\Lambda}, 𝒖∘\bm{u}^{\circ}, 𝚲β\bm{\Lambda}_{\beta} are Tinv, u_const, Tw; and 𝒑\bm{p}, 𝒖\bm{u}, 𝑽~\widetilde{\bm{V}} are p, u, uv.

A8.8  Backward pass

The backward pass follows the forward decomposition chunk by chunk in reverse order. Let d​𝑯∈ℝC×dv\mathrm{d}\bm{H}\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times d_{v}} and d​𝑺C∈ℝdv×dk\mathrm{d}\bm{S}_{C}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{v}\times d_{k}} be the upstream gradients of a chunk, the latter including the gradient d​𝑺0\mathrm{d}\bm{S}_{0} returned by the following chunk. Write 𝒈:=𝒄−𝜷⊙𝒑\bm{g}:=\bm{c}-\bm{\beta}\odot\bm{p} and 𝒀0:=𝑽​𝑺0∈ℝC×dk\bm{Y}_{0}:=\bm{V}\bm{S}_{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times d_{k}}. With stril\operatorname{stril} and tril\operatorname{tril} the strictly lower and the lower triangular part, the vector–Jacobian products of (A158) and (A159) are

d​𝑺0\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\bm{S}_{0} =d​𝑺C​𝚪C+d​𝑯⊤​𝑸^,\displaystyle=\mathrm{d}\bm{S}_{C}\bm{\Gamma}_{C}+\mathrm{d}\bm{H}^{\top}\widehat{\bm{Q}}, d​𝜸C\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\bm{\gamma}_{C} =(d​𝑺C⊙𝑺0)⊤​𝟏,\displaystyle=(\mathrm{d}\bm{S}_{C}\odot\bm{S}_{0})^{\top}\bm{1}, d​𝑲˘\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\breve{\bm{K}} =𝑽~​d​𝑺C,\displaystyle=\widetilde{\bm{V}}\,\mathrm{d}\bm{S}_{C},
d​𝑽~\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\widetilde{\bm{V}} =𝑲˘​d​𝑺C⊤+𝑮q​k⊤​d​𝑯,\displaystyle=\breve{\bm{K}}\,\mathrm{d}\bm{S}_{C}^{\top}+\bm{G}^{qk\top}\mathrm{d}\bm{H}, d​𝑸^\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\widehat{\bm{Q}} =d​𝑯​𝑺0,\displaystyle=\mathrm{d}\bm{H}\,\bm{S}_{0}, d​𝑮q​k\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\bm{G}^{qk} =tril⁡(d​𝑯​𝑽~⊤),\displaystyle=\operatorname{tril}(\mathrm{d}\bm{H}\,\widetilde{\bm{V}}^{\top}), (A162)

those of the pseudo-values and of the solve (A156) are

d​𝒖\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\bm{u} =(d​𝑽~⊙𝑽)​𝟏,\displaystyle=(\mathrm{d}\widetilde{\bm{V}}\odot\bm{V})\bm{1}, d​𝑽\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\bm{V} +=diag(𝒖)d𝑽~,\displaystyle\mathrel{+}=\operatorname{diag}(\bm{u})\,\mathrm{d}\widetilde{\bm{V}}, d​𝚲\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\bm{\Lambda} =d​𝒖​𝒈⊤,\displaystyle=\mathrm{d}\bm{u}\,\bm{g}^{\top}, d​𝒈\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\bm{g} =𝚲⊤​d​𝒖,\displaystyle=\bm{\Lambda}^{\top}\mathrm{d}\bm{u},

those of the scores (A157) and of the Gram matrices (A152), (A155) are

and the decay-scaled copies (A151) and the cumulative sum (A150) give

d​𝜸\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\bm{\gamma} =d𝑲^⊙𝑲−d𝑲¯⊙𝑲/𝜸2+d𝑸^⊙𝑸−d𝑲˘⊙𝑲⊙𝜸C/𝜸2,d𝜸C+=(d𝑲˘⊙𝑲/𝜸)⊤𝟏,\displaystyle=\mathrm{d}\widehat{\bm{K}}\odot\bm{K}-\mathrm{d}\bar{\bm{K}}\odot\bm{K}/\bm{\gamma}^{2}+\mathrm{d}\widehat{\bm{Q}}\odot\bm{Q}-\mathrm{d}\breve{\bm{K}}\odot\bm{K}\odot\bm{\gamma}_{C}/\bm{\gamma}^{2},\qquad\mathrm{d}\bm{\gamma}_{C}\mathrel{+}=\big(\mathrm{d}\breve{\bm{K}}\odot\bm{K}/\bm{\gamma}\big)^{\top}\bm{1},
d​ℓr\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\bm{\ell}_{r} =d𝜸r⊙𝜸r+𝟙[r=C]d𝜸C⊙𝜸C,dlog𝐟i=∑r≥idℓr(reverse cumulative sum).\displaystyle=\mathrm{d}\bm{\gamma}_{r}\odot\bm{\gamma}_{r}+\mathbbm{1}[r=C]\;\mathrm{d}\bm{\gamma}_{C}\odot\bm{\gamma}_{C},\qquad\mathrm{d}\log\mathbf{f}_{i}=\sum_{r\geq i}\mathrm{d}\bm{\ell}_{r}\quad\text{(reverse cumulative sum).} (A165)

Here 𝜸∈ℝC×dk\bm{\gamma}\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times d_{k}} stacks the 𝜸r\bm{\gamma}_{r} and all products with it are element-wise. Two points differ from the delta-rule backward. The values enter the system matrix 𝑵\bm{N} through 𝑮v​v\bm{G}^{vv}, so d​𝑽\mathrm{d}\bm{V} receives a contribution through the inverse in (A163)–(A164), whereas in DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet and KDA the values appear only in the right-hand side. And since the pseudo-values are ur​𝒗ru_{r}\bm{v}_{r}, the gradient with respect to the write coefficients is the row-wise contraction d​𝒖=(d​𝑽~⊙𝑽)​𝟏\mathrm{d}\bm{u}=(\mathrm{d}\widetilde{\bm{V}}\odot\bm{V})\bm{1} over the value dimension, mirroring the forward contraction that produces 𝒑\bm{p}. The gate factor diag⁡(𝜷)\operatorname{diag}(\bm{\beta}) sits inside the Hadamard product and must be kept inside the accumulation of d​𝑵\mathrm{d}\bm{N}, as observed for the channel-wise gates of Gated DeltaNet-2 (Hatamizadeh et al., 2026).

A8.9  Verification

We verified Theorem A11 and (A162)–(A165) numerically in double precision against the token-by-token recurrence (A149): outputs and final memory agree to machine precision (≤10−15\leq 10^{-15} relative) for chunk lengths C∈{1,8,16,L}C\in\{1,8,16,L\}, sequence lengths that are and are not multiples of CC, dk≠dvd_{k}\neq d_{v}, nonzero initial memory, strong and weak decay, and βr∈(0,1)\beta_{r}\in(0,1) as well as βr∈(0,2)\beta_{r}\in(0,2); the operator identity (A161) holds against the explicitly formed product of dk​dv×dk​dvd_{k}d_{v}\times d_{k}d_{v} factors; the no-decay reduction of 𝑵\bm{N} to the Gram of 𝒂r=𝒌r⊗𝒗r\bm{a}_{r}=\bm{k}_{r}\otimes\bm{v}_{r} holds; and the gradients with respect to 𝑸,𝑲,𝑽,𝜷,𝒄,log⁡𝐟\bm{Q},\bm{K},\bm{V},\bm{\beta},\bm{c},\log\mathbf{f} and 𝑺0\bm{S}_{0} agree with central finite differences of the recurrence to 10−910^{-9}. The reference implementations in the supplementary material are checked against the same recurrence.
